annotations.keyFindings: Among patients ruled out at one hour (57 percent of those tested), 30-day death or myocardial infarction was 0.3 percent across 22 studies; sensitivity for index infarction 98.8 percent.
annotations.limitations: Search ended June 2021; mostly specialist centres; eight studies at high risk of selection bias; few results by age or kidney function.

annotations.keyFindings: In a district hospital, time in the department for ruled-out patients fell from 7.2 to 4.1 hours with unchanged 30-day events; early sample timing errors fell after a phlebotomy prompt.
annotations.limitations: Uncontrolled before-after comparison in one hospital; secular changes not addressed.

annotations.keyFindings: Second samples fell outside the 45 to 75 minute window in 18 percent of patients; late samples placed more patients in the observe zone.
annotations.limitations: Three departments; outcome follow-up for late-sampled patients only partly reported.

annotations.keyFindings: Sensitivity stayed above 97 percent in older and kidney patients, but only 29 and 21 percent were ruled out at one hour against 62 percent of younger patients.
annotations.limitations: Specialist centres; kidney function from a single measurement.

annotations.keyFindings: Reported 0.2 percent 30-day death or myocardial infarction among 7,950 patients discharged within four hours after one-hour rule-out.
annotations.limitations: Conference abstract only: follow-up methods not described, capture outside the region unclear and no full report; grade withheld until a full report is available.

claims.text: Among patients ruled out at one hour, the 30-day rate of death or myocardial infarction was 0.3 percent across 22 studies.
claims.passage: the 30-day rate of death or myocardial infarction was 0.3 percent (95 percent CI 0.2 to 0.5)
claims.interpretation: Safety at 30 days is well estimated for the populations studied, mostly younger patients in specialist centres.

claims.text: After a district hospital switched to a one-hour pathway, median time in the department for ruled-out patients fell from 7.2 to 4.1 hours.
claims.passage: Median time in the department for ruled-out patients fell from 7.2 to 4.1 hours
claims.interpretation: A planning value for time saved in a comparable hospital; uncontrolled.

claims.text: Under a one-hour algorithm, the second sample was collected outside the 45 to 75 minute window in 18 percent of patients.
claims.passage: The second sample was collected outside the 45 to 75 minute window in 18 percent of patients
claims.interpretation: Sample timing is the main practical failure point; the review should report it and what reduced it.

claims.text: Only 29 percent of patients aged 75 or over and 21 percent of patients with kidney disease were ruled out at one hour.
claims.passage: only 29 percent of older patients and 21 percent of patients with kidney disease were ruled out at one hour
claims.interpretation: The time saving will be much smaller for the older patients who make up 38 percent of attendances.

synthesis: Five retrieved records, appraised at abstract level; the regional conference abstract is kept as context but not graded, because its follow-up methods are not described. A meta-analysis of 22 studies found 0.3 percent 30-day death or myocardial infarction among patients ruled out at one hour, and a district hospital halved time in the department after switching pathways. Second samples drawn outside the timing window are common, and rule-out at one hour is far less frequent in older patients and in kidney disease.
gradeRationale: Unchanged: consistent safety estimates from many studies, downgraded once for indirectness to an older district hospital population; the ungraded conference abstract does not contribute to certainty.
summary: Re-appraisal on the investigator's request: the conference abstract's grade is withdrawn (explicit null); other annotations, the four claims and the overall certainty are unchanged.
